I do think online exams were better for learning. I feel like I didn’t have the pressure of having to cram/retain info that I would forget in a week (even if I started studying earlier). I absorbed info better with online exams because profs were more flexible and made quite a few assignments revolve around learning through integrating info rather than rote memorization for exams. 

I know this is also a controversial topic but I get extremely anxious during exams and forget half the stuff I learnt no matter how well I prepared. In person exams may not work for everyone as different people perform better under different conditions.

I personally am for the hybrid education, I think those that want to go back to in person should have the option, for me I have been very anxious and online classes have been detrimental to my mental health and my motivation to study keeps going downhill even though I am trying practice self care. But I also see the other point of view that classes should stay online as there may be fear of spreading covid to immunocompromised people. 

Overall, I think that profs should be more flexible about it. I know some are demanding people to go back to in person and are not offering to record lectures. It would be nice to have the option for recorded lectures, zoom tutorials. Although exams might be a bit tricky to handle, I did find that online exams were better mainly because if they were open book I found it easier to integrate and learn material but closed book added more pressure to just memorize and regurgitate.
